argument_summary: The certification defense should be read narrowly. The admissible record supports overall launch readiness and supports treating the developer-support migration miss as a bounded, explicitly documented limitation rather than a release-wide failure. It does not support claiming clean policy satisfaction for launch without further qualification, because the affected segment is a named launch use case, legal review is still open, and there is no admissible evidence here of completed disclosure or approved pre-launch risk acceptance. On that record, the supportable position is qualified certification with the limitation stated plainly and tracked through deployment, not an unqualified compliance claim.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost claim is needed to justify the requested treatment. The argument stands on the admissible record and on narrowing the certification claim to a qualified basis.
claims_about_policy: Policy is the limiting issue. The admissible evidence supports saying aggregate readiness and monitoring principles are relevant but not dispositive. The policy text makes named launch use cases material, and pending legal review leaves that predicate unresolved rather than satisfied. The correct reading is that the packet can support a caveated certification posture only if it is understood as documenting a known limitation and not as proving that disclosure or approved risk acceptance already occurred.
concessions: Aggregate readiness and no severity-one rehearsal incidents do not, by themselves, satisfy the separate policy condition for a material limitation affecting a named launch use case.
The developer-support migration segment is named in a partner launch checklist, which weighs toward materiality under the policy text.
The legal disclosure question remains open on the admissible record.
There is no admissible evidence here of completed disclosure or approved pre-launch risk acceptance.
